## Trial `package-version-hold-ubuntu16__vgUiFGB`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor satisfied both material outcomes of the task: curl was placed on apt-mark hold at its currently installed version, and a dist-upgrade dry-run directly confirmed curl is excluded from the upgrade set both before and after a full node reboot, showing the hold persists across a restart. The reboot cycle (boot_id 9094f607... -> c66c32d0...) also satisfies the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol with a clean pre/post transition and no residue. All commands are read-only checks or narrowly scoped, purposeful mutations directly tied to the task or the restart protocol.

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** curl package is held at its current installed version (7.47.0-1ubuntu2.19) on node1
  - **Why:** Executor confirmed the installed curl version, ran 'sudo apt-mark hold curl' (returned 'curl set on hold.'), and verified curl appears in apt-mark showhold output and dpkg selections show 'hold'. Post-restart re-check (dpkg -l shows 'hi' status flag) confirms the hold is durable, not just applied and forgotten.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b48b4315f2c84a4f`, `cmd-48f1e9abddba478e`, `cmd-707e64d09ccf4ea1`, `cmd-f1943d0e5fa042b2`, `cmd-8136f8743c1d42ce`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** A system update (dist-upgrade) leaves curl at its current version, i.e. does not attempt to upgrade it
  - **Why:** After apt-get update, a dist-upgrade dry-run (--simulate) was run and grepped for curl, returning no match (grep exit 1) even though many other packages were listed as being configured/upgraded. apt-cache policy also shows the candidate version equals the installed version, and post-reboot the dry-run again excludes curl, directly demonstrating the hold is effective against the package manager's upgrade path.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-382550ac4d784ce3`, `cmd-7f84984aa1fb4eef`, `cmd-bf85c9cbbb474d47`, `cmd-8136f8743c1d42ce`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **1.000**. Every state-changing command has a clear purpose: apt-mark hold curl (the task's core action), apt-get update (necessary prerequisite for a meaningful dist-upgrade simulation), and the reboot (shutdown -r now) which is part of the separate provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol rather than an unnecessary mutation, since it was bounded, non-destructive, and used only to demonstrate persistence of the hold. The dist-upgrade commands were run with -s (simulate/dry-run) and did not actually mutate installed packages. Lifecycle diffs show only expected reboot artifacts (new boot_id, new systemd-private temp dirs replacing old ones) with no leftover files, no failed services, and unchanged package-health status before and after. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-48f1e9abddba478e`, `cmd-02aa4213b6ab469d`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services`
